The Crescent Moon Spring, known as Shajing in ancient times and commonly known as Medicine Spring, is located at the western end of the Hexi Corridor in Gansu Province, 5 kilometers southwest of Dunhuang City and 7 kilometers south of the city at the northern foot of Mount Mingsha. The company has been in the business since the Han Dynasty as one of the "eight scenes of Dunhuang", named "Yuequan Xiaoqing". The moon crescent spring is nearly 100 meters long from north to south and 25 meters wide from east to west. The spring is deep in the east and shallow in the west, with a depth of about 5 meters at its deepest point, bending like a crescent moon, hence its name, and is known as the "first spring in the desert. The Moon Crescent Spring Scenic Spot of Mingsha Mountain. It covers an area of 31,200 square kilometers, including the Mingsha Mountain, which is more than 40 kilometers long from east to west and about 20 kilometers wide from north to south, with the main peak at an altitude of 1,715 meters. The crescent moon spring is surrounded by the Mingsha Mountain. It is known for its wonderful landscape of "mountains and springs living together, sand and water coexisting", and is known as "one of the best scenery outside of China", and is one of the "two best" in the south of Dunhuang, where the Ming Sha Mountain, the Crescent Moon Spring and the Mogao Caves are integrated into one artistic landscape. It has become a popular tourist destination in China and the world. The main attractions are the Moon Tooth Spring and the Ming Sha Mountain. The crescent moon spring is surrounded by the Mingsha Mountain, and its shape resembles a crescent moon, hence its name. Ming Sha Mountain is located 5 kilometers from the southern suburbs of Dunhuang City, named after the sound of the sand moving into. It is made of quicksand and is divided into five colors: red, yellow, green, white and black. In 1994, it was designated as a national key scenic spot and won the honorary title of "one of the five most beautiful deserts in China". Tickets: 120 yuan (three days per person)

It is an ancient altar built by a schist, inside for the idol of the Dragon Five, there is a spring well in front of the altar, above and below the garden, the spring water does not dry up all year long taste sweet and clear heart. In the southwestern part of Shanghai, Songjiang District, there is a historical site that is not very well known, but its discovery has painted a big part of Shanghai's history: Guangfulin Heritage Park. Shanghai Guangfu Forest, formerly known as Huangfu Forest. It is said that more than 6,000 years ago, the ancestors of Songjiang flourished in the area of Guangfulin. By 4000 years ago, the earliest group of immigrants from the Yellow River Basin came here and created the Guangfulin culture together with the people who lived here. It is said that there was Songjiang Province first, and then there was Shanghai Beach; there was Guangfulin first, and then there was the history of Songjiang". The Guangfulin site was discovered in 1958, a trial excavation was conducted in 1961, and the official excavation was carried out from October 1999 to January 2000, covering a total area of more than 40,000 square meters. The discovery of the Guangfulin site gained the archaeological name of "Guangfulin Culture" and filled the gap in the cultural spectrum of the late Neolithic period in the lower reaches of the Yangtze River. (The historical gap between "Liangzhu culture" and "Maqiao culture") The Guangfulin site has been renovated over the years and is now a cultural park open to the public - Guangfulin Heritage Park. Among the many parks in Shanghai, there are not many parks with real traces of history. The core of the park is a pyramid-shaped museum with modern Chinese architecture floating in the lake. The precipitation of history always speaks of the glorious past without words.
